bridges.why: the previous episode ends 'Remember that name', then 93 blocks of cavern pass before Gumil appears; this at least hands the reader back

bridges.after: If you do, it will go well for both you and me. I swear it on

bridges.ko: 맹세는 성문이 열릴 때까지만 간다. 그다음엔 살육이 시작된다. 품석은 제 차례를 기다리지 않는다.
bridges.why: Pumsuk surrenders on an oath and the next line is the herald announcing him dead; the broken oath and his death are never shown

stories.logline: Gumil, a yellow-sleeve clerk with a wife every man stares at and pay that buys her nothing, wants to count for something in a country that ranks bones; a True Bone boy is put over him at Daeya, and the episode ends with that boy unable to sleep after watching Maehwa at the feast.
stories.fixes: The title character first appears at block 96 of 136. Blocks 0–92 are Yushin at the steam cavern (including a 75-block First Kim flashback that the Seohyun episode will also tell), then BOTH ROADS and Chunchu's steam visit. The previous episode ended on 'Its grain clerk is called Gumil. Remember that name…!', so the reader lands in the wrong story. Move blocks 0–92 into their own cavern episode, and merge them with the other steam scenes scattered through Siege of Daeya (61–78) and Forty Fortresses (12–22). Open on Gumil's own line ('Putting a boy this green in charge of the border…' works as a provocation). Cut block 94: Euija sending Yunchung is already told in Yunchung. Move block 95 ('Pumsuk is the head general') down to sit before 127, because 116 says the True Bone hasn't arrived yet. The two passages of Maehwa walking past staring men (108–114 and 116–120) are the same beat twice, so keep one. The couple's last good night (121–126) is the emotional spine and should sit just before the arrival. The Pumsuk-on-the-pallet ending is a good hand-off to Maehwa.

stories.logline: Pumsuk, twenty-four and married, tries to sleep instead of going back to Maehwa; he fails, and she means to teach him a lesson and ruin him a little, but ends up undone and in love; he walks out without a word, and her husband comes home.
stories.fixes: The opener ('A man is measured by his self-control') and the turn (the teacher's voice dying, the slip of his wife's name at 48–49) give it a real shape, and it stays in one place. The middle (57–74) repeats the same escalation cycle five or six times, so the stakes (Gumil at the stores, Gotaso, the fortress) drop out for the back half. Cut that run by half and keep one beat where she remembers her husband is only at the stores. The record quote (81) retells what we just watched, so cut it or move it to Siege of Daeya. The ending (he leaves without a word, then 'Morning comes. So does her husband') is a strong hand-off.

stories.logline: Gumil makes his wife tell him everything, and three weeks later he opens the granary gate to Baekje; Daeya falls, Gotaso goes with the fetch, Pumsuk surrenders on an oath and dies anyway, and Chunchu, who made him swear to protect her, asks for the road north.
stories.fixes: The core is strong: the 'everyone in this fortress is trash' callback, Gotaso and Kangrim, and Chunchu on his mother's knee. The order around the fall is scrambled. Block 40 (the news reaches the queen) comes before 41–42 (Pumsuk and Yunchung negotiating at Daeya), then 43 is back in Surabol. Move 40 after 42 and show the broken oath (bridge proposed). Mochuk (19) and Jukjuk (quote 46) appear with no setup: give Jukjuk one line in the siege or cut the quote. The episode runs on past its natural end. After Chunchu asks for the road north (56), the Bupmin gate scene (57–60) is fine, but STEAM, AGAIN (61–78) is another cavern visit. Move it to the cavern episode so this one ends on Silla's grief and the road to Pyongyang.

stories.logline: Yeon Gesomun has bowed all summer for his father's seal and has been given one winter on the border; at a banquet with the king he closes every door, takes the five commanders' swords onto his own back, crowns a puppet and makes himself Supreme Commander, then promises his wife none of what the world says matters.
stories.fixes: It works as its own story, with a clear want, a clear humiliation, a turn and a quiet ending. Fixes: the Bojang 'what is your name?' beat (51–53) comes after Bojang is already crowned (41–43). Move it before 41 so we watch Yeon pick the puppet. The massacre is told in a speech, then four record quotes (35, 36, 50, 54). Keep one, maybe two. The Taoist turn (55–59) is told again in Four Dragons ('The Third Leg'), so keep it in one place. The first line is a date and a death. A sharper hook would be something like 'All summer, Yeon bows.'

stories.logline: Chunchu, grieving his daughter, goes north to beg troops from the man who just murdered his king; Yeon names a price Chunchu won't pay, Chunchu bleeds and is jailed, a drunk favourite's turtle-and-rabbit story gives him the way out, and Yushin's march gets him released.
stories.fixes: The setup (sixty days, Hadong, 'It's you I don't trust') and the turtle story are excellent. The withheld hand wound pays off in the next episode. The ending is scrambled. 53 (Yushin counts men), 54 (narration says Yeon releases him), 55–58 (Chunchu and Yushin swapping lines before they have met), 59–62 (the reunion), then 64–68 (Yeon deciding to release him, played out a second time). Reorder it as 53 → 64–68 → 55–56, 58 (Chunchu let out) → 59–62, put Yushin's quip (57) inside the camp, and cut 54. Say the price aloud (bridge proposed). The opening news beat ('murdered by his own subject?') is repeated word for word by Euija in the next episode, so change one of them.

stories.logline: Euija goes to Pyongyang himself to buy the man who killed his king; they fight over whether kings and sun-gods are real, Euija wins Yeon with a harbour plan to cut Silla off, and Yeon admits that Euija and Chunchu frighten him the same way.
stories.fixes: The debate (politics as alchemy, the sun god) and the Chunchu-hand flashback are the episode. The journey is missing, though: block 3 is in Sabi and block 4 is at Yeon's door, so add a bridge. Euija's first line copies Sunduk's from the previous episode. 'You came with three. You're leaving with five' (49) is said before the two maids appear (51), so set up the three attendants on arrival or move 49–50 after 59. The maid tail (51–59) dilutes the ending. End instead on 'I do not yet know which of you frightens me more' / 'Flattery' / 'It was not flattery,' then the ride south (60).

stories.logline: Yushin, thirty-four, a banner captain on a nameless horse, asks his father to let him be the collar; three charges later he sets a general's head at his father's feet, names the horse Hangyul, and in Pyongyang a Yeon father warns his son about the name.
stories.fixes: It works as a standalone, and the jump into it is set up by Euija & Yeon's last line. The only confusion is the cut from the Silla command post to the Pyongyang court (14–15), so add the header. Yeon Taejo's 'At the Colossal River' is a plant the Colossal River episode never pays off. Put young Taejo with the rolled Sui banner in that episode.

stories.logline: Yushin takes more than forty Baekje fortresses, Euija panics at his name, and the cavern sisters give him three answers.
stories.fixes: This is a montage with no scene and no turn. The entry's place is set to steam_cavern. Euija's panic (1–3) has no room or listener. The Yushin–Chunchu exchange (8–10) floats. The cavern visit is the fourth in four episodes, and the closing Euija line (23) has no context. Its time is also out of order: 'over the next few years' with a 644 map, then The Eastern Star goes back to 642. Rebuild it around one scene. The best candidate is the record at quote 11, where Yushin rides past his own gate and asks only for a cup of water from home. Grow his reputation through Baekje soldiers who stop eating at his name. Move the cavern beat out and set the entry's place to the border.

stories.logline: On one bright night three men (Chunchu in Surabol, Euija in Sabi, Gesomun at the sacred cave) each say out loud that they want to be the King for All.
stories.fixes: The triptych and its refrain are good. But it opens on a bare dialogue line with no place, then cuts twice with no header. Add a one-line narrator opener (e.g. 'One star, three roofs, three men who can't sleep.'). Gyebek's 'I saw Gesomun again' and the burn scar (13–14) are a plant: make sure it fires in a later Gyebek episode, or cut it.

stories.logline: Far to the west, the emperor who owns half the world hears that a man called Gai Suwen has murdered his king.
stories.fixes: It is a seven-block stub, and Four Dragons replays the same beat (the report, then 'Wait. Gai Suwen…?' at block 19). Merge it into Four Dragons as the cold open and cut Four Dragons 17–21. Or keep Emperor and remove the report from Four Dragons. Don't tell it twice.

stories.logline: The Second Emperor, whose name no one may say, loses the one minister allowed to say no, hears Yeon's name and decides to lead the seventh invasion himself; meanwhile Silla's envoy is offered a borrowed king and a Longmen farmer is sent off to war by his wife.
stories.fixes: Taizong's want (to undo four hundred barbarian years and not repeat the Sui) is clear. Wei Zheng's death is a good obstacle that removes itself. The rest is three side stories. 'The Third Leg' repeats Yeon's Massacre 55–59, so cut it here. 'Three Choices' is a useful plant for Bidam. Longmen (47–68) is Xue Rengui's origin and would open Stallion Mountain better, where block 0 already repeats block 68. Block 20 tells the Yeon Tabal/Jolbon story before Jolbon opens it, so cut it. The 'herald' speakers (5–6) need an owner (bridge proposed).

stories.logline: The Blue Dragon walks around Goguryeo's wall of forts; Yodong, which never opened for the Sui, dresses a girl as a bride for the Holy King and still falls in twelve days.
stories.fixes: The fall of Yodong is a complete arc: the ford trick, the marsh road, the bride, the south wind. Then 15–19 jump to Ansi for the emperor and the Guardian's face-off, which spends the Ansi episode's central exchange early. 'The Rest of the Line' (20–23) then goes back in time to the fourth and fifth months. Move 14–19 into Ansi and end Yodong on the burning tower and the rest of the line. The bride (9) needs one line of setup earlier in the siege so her four words land.

stories.logline: King Dongchun wins twice against an imperial general, rides out to win a third time on ground he never looked at, and loses his capital in an afternoon.
stories.fixes: It works as a short parable, and Yodong's last line sets up the jump in. The lesson ('I did not look at the ground') should fire in Stallion Mountain: give the Goguryeo relief commander one beat of not looking at the ground. Quote 9 calls the king 'Gung' with no gloss, which may read as a different man.

stories.logline: A farmer in white armour breaks the Goguryeo relief army and wins the emperor's favour; a Silla exile in the Tang ranks dies farther in than anyone; the farmer is captured and escapes; and Yeon's two small sons are offered titles, and the elder takes the flogging for both.
stories.fixes: There are three stories with three protagonists. Xue Rengui's arc (field to fame) is the spine, and the Longmen setup from Four Dragons should open this episode. Block 0 already duplicates Four Dragons 68. Sul Gedu is called 'Captain Xue' right before Xue Rengui appears, so rename that line or add the bridge. The capture-and-escape (26–38) restages Xue's heroism a second time and could be cut. Namseng and Namgun (39–49) are a strong plant for Brothers' Coup, but they have nothing to do with this battle's story. Move them to a flashback there or to the Ansi retreat.

stories.logline: Ulchi Munduk surrenders seven times and runs seven times, drawing the Sui army to within thirty li of Pyongyang, then breaks it halfway across the Salsu.
stories.fixes: The jump in is set up well ('a general who surrendered seven times'), but nothing happens on stage. It is all edicts, maps, a formation and record quotes, and Munduk never speaks. Block 0 is a textbook date ('in the year 612'). Give it one scene: Munduk walking into the Sui camp (5), with the poem (8) as the letter he hands Yu Zhongwen. Put Yeon Taejo, Gesomun's father, in the Goguryeo line, riding home with a Sui banner under his arm. That pays off Nangbi 23–25, where Gesomun remembers it from when he was seven.

stories.logline: The nameless Guardian, who once kept the old king's colours on his wall in Yeon's face, holds one small fortress against the emperor; the earthen mountain falls into his wall, his men take it, winter starves the horses, and the emperor sends silk to a man whose name he never learns.
stories.fixes: It stands on its own. Bring the emperor–Guardian face-off back from Yodong 15–19, because it is this episode's argument. The arrow-and-helmet beat (24) doesn't say whose head it is (bridge proposed). 'The ring at his hip' (7) is also ambiguous. The aside about a Silla marshal (8) and 'added to the Great Heroes' (30) are textbook lines and could go. Move his last line ('you will never be crazier than we are', 35) to just before the silk (32) so the episode ends on the bow from the wall.

stories.logline: Yuhwa, the youngest river-daughter, stays in the water when the sun god stops his chariot; she takes him into a copper room on the bank, her father throws her out, a fox leads her to Buyeo's king, and she lays an egg nobody can break.
stories.fixes: Ansi's last line sets up the jump into it. But it is Yuhwa's story under Haemosu's name, and Haemosu's exit is never shown. The quote at 70 says he left and never came back, yet his voice guides her at 64. Add one beat of him going back to the chariot and the hour resuming, so his later rescues in Buyeo and Jolbon read as a debt. Mark the arrival in Buyeo (header proposed).

stories.logline: Jumong hatches from the egg and outshoots the princes who feed him; his mother's needle wins him the fastest horse, Daeso's knife misses, and with the river ahead and death written down for the day, his father catches the reaper's wrist and the turtles make a road.
stories.fixes: It is a complete tale, and the cavern prayer and Sosuno hook make a good card. Mark the time skips (grown men, the side room, the stable, the knife). Galsa founding his own country (25) spends a future the story never uses, so cut it or keep it to one clause. Haemosu's 'my little brother … at his new job' (67) means nothing to a first-time reader. Lady Ye's 'leave the door half open' is a good plant and needs its payoff in a later Yuri beat.

stories.logline: Jumong, a wet exile on his knees in Tabal's hall, is made a slave to the chief's widowed daughter Sosuno; she fights wanting him all the way to a confession at the well, he splits Tabal's arrow, unites five feuding roofs, and is voted first king, with his father finally showing his face at dawn.
stories.fixes: The Sosuno romance (scenes through the hundred-paces test) is a strong standalone arc. The last forty blocks scatter it: the Pine Kingdom, a flash-forward to Jumong's death (236), Haemosu at dawn, the two sons, Sosuno's 'founding a country twice' line (252, which opens the Onjo box early), a flashback to Yuhwa's death 'five winters before' placed after scenes years later, a life-summary of Jumong's death, and an aside about the Yeon hall. End on Haemosu's dawn ('Build a world of your own') or on the Two Sons plant. Move Yuhwa's death before the dawn so the sun god comes to his son straight from her. Cut 236 and 252. Sosuno gets two cards (26 and 42), so keep one. The next-episode card ('the queen is failing… lock the door') doesn't match Gi, which opens on Chunchu sailing east. Rewrite it to tease the voyage, and mark the leap from myth back to 645.
